Kuvitus: fysiikan luokan pöytä. Pöydällä: Illustration: a physics classroom table. On the table is a cart carrying two metal masses. A string tied to the cart passes over a pulley at the edge of the table, and a single metal mass hangs from the other end of the string. A measuring scale and a stopwatch lie on the table, and a student stands beside it.
Two bodies and their free-body diagrams. On the left, the situation: a cart on a table, and a string tied to it passes over a pulley at the table's edge to a hanging mass. Above the cart are thin arrows: a blue velocity to the right and a shorter orange acceleration to the right. Top right, the free-body diagram of the cart, drawn as a rectangle: weight G1 down from the centre, the normal force N from the table up from the bottom surface and as long as the weight, and the tension T1 in the string to the right from the right edge. Bottom right, the free-body diagram of the hanging mass: weight G2 down from the centre and the tension T2 in the string up from the top surface. The arrow T2 is shorter than G2, and the arrows T1 and T2 are equally long.
Esimerkin kärry ja riippuva punnus. Vase: The cart and hanging mass of the example. On the left, the situation: the cart on the table, the string over a pulley to the hanging mass, and above the cart a blue velocity and an orange acceleration to the right. Top right, the free-body diagram of the cart: weight G1 down, the equally long normal force N up and the tension T1 to the right. Bottom right, the free-body diagram of the hanging mass: weight G2 down and the shorter tension T2 up. The arrows T1 and T2 are equally long.
Kaksi riippuvaa kappaletta ja niiden voi: Two hanging bodies and their free-body diagrams. On the left, the situation: a string passes over a pulley hanging from the ceiling, with a lighter body on its left end and a heavier one on its right end. Beside the lighter body is an orange arrow up and beside the heavier one an equally long orange arrow down: the acceleration has the same magnitude. Top right, the free-body diagram of the lighter body, drawn as a rectangle: tension T1 up from the top surface and weight G1 down from the centre, with T1 longer than G1. Bottom right, the free-body diagram of the heavier body: T2 up from the top surface and G2 down from the centre, with G2 longer than T2. The arrows T1 and T2 are equally long.
Opiskelijan piirtämä voimakuvio pöydällä: A student's free-body diagram of a cart on a table, tied with a string over a pulley to a hanging mass. The cart is a rectangle. From its centre an arrow G1 points down, and from its bottom surface an equally long arrow N points up. From the right edge of the cart an arrow G2 points to the right; it is shorter than G1 and as long as the weight of the hanging mass. There are no other arrows.
Mallikuvio: kaksi riippuvaa kappaletta,: Model diagram: two hanging bodies, 0.40 kg and 0.80 kg, at the ends of a string over a pulley. On the left, the situation, where the lighter body rises and the heavier one descends, and orange arrows show the accelerations. Top right, the free-body diagram of the lighter body: tension T1 up, longer than the weight G1 down. Bottom right, the free-body diagram of the heavier body: tension T2 up and a longer weight G2 down. The arrows T1 and T2 are equally long.
Mallikuvio: kaksi laatikkoa roikkuu köys: Model diagram: two crates hang one below the other on ropes and rise with increasing speed. On the left, the situation: a crane's rope holds the upper crate, and the lower crate hangs from a second rope under the upper one. An orange arrow shows the acceleration upward. Top right, the free-body diagram of the upper crate: the tension T1 in the crane's rope up, the weight G1 down from the centre and the tension T2 in the lower rope down from the bottom surface. Bottom right, the free-body diagram of the lower crate: the tension T2 in the rope up from the top surface and the weight G2 down. The arrow T1 is the longest, and T2 is equally long in both diagrams.
